items.text: Say goodbye to brown bananas! Gene-edited fruits could soon be sold in UK supermarkets
items.article: Experts at Tropic Biosciences, a UK company based in Norfolk, used a technique known as CRISPR-Cas9 to edit three genes that cause bananas to brown. By XANTHA LEATHAM, EXECUTIVE SCIENCE EDITOR Published: 10:09, 28 September 2026 | Updated: 16:04, 28 September 2026 Tired of bananas turning brown before you’ve had the chance to eat them? The infuriating problem could soon be a thing of the past – after scientists developed a gene-edited variety that stays fresher for longer. Experts at a British firm used a laboratory technique called CRISPR to tweak three genes that cause the fruit to brown. It means the bananas will last for up to day once they have been peeled or cut – and that they will last longer and better be able to withstand bumps and bruises.

items.article: From bringing scorched lawns back to life to improving soil so it holds on to more moisture, experts share their top tips for helping UK gardens recover from the relentless summer heat. Daily Mail journalists select and curate the products that feature on our site. If you make a purchase via links on this page we will earn commission - learn more After weeks of relentless heat, long dry spells and plenty of sunshine, the UK is finally getting some much-needed relief from a summer of back-to-back heatwaves. Temperatures are set to drop from the 30s to the mid-20s in many parts of the country this week, with showers and the chance of thunderstorms bringing cooler, wetter weather. Parts of Kent, Essex and Sussex have already seen some light or patchy rain overnight, offering a welcome break after all three counties were officially declared to be in drought on July 29. But experts warn that a little rain won’t be enough to undo months of dry weather. For green-fingered homeowners who have watched their lawns turn straw-coloured and plants struggle in the heat, the cooler weather means it's finally time to start giving their gardens some TLC.

items.article: Galgotias University achieves remarkable success, climbing to 41st in India in THE World University Rankings 2027 and entering the 1001-1200 global band. Discover its rise among top private institutions & strong international standing in QS 2027. Galgotias University Soars 24 Places to Rank 41st in India in Times Higher Education World University Rankings 2027. Enters India’s top 20 private institutions and advances to the 1001-1200 global band; QS 2027 recognition strengthens its international standing. Greater Noida, 30 September 2026: Galgotias University has climbed 24 places to 41st among all universities in India in the Times Higher Education (THE) World University Rankings 2027, released today. The University was ranked 65th in the 2026 edition. Among private universities and institutions in India, Galgotias has risen seven places to 20th, from 27th last year. Globally, it has moved up from the 1201-1500 band to the 1001-1200 band. The achievement adds to the University’s recognition in the QS World University Rankings 2027, where Galgotias is placed in the 1201-1400 global band, ranking 16th among private universities in India, 46th among all Indian universities and third among private universities in Uttar Pradesh. Its presence in both THE and QS world rankings marks an important milestone in its development as an internationally recognised institution. The 2027 edition ranks 2,297 universities from 118 countries and territories, up from 2,191 last year.
